title: Animal models for anxiety-like and depression-like behavior
protocol: Fill a 19 cm diameter glass cylinder with water to a depth of 10 cm, maintaining the temperature between 23-25 ºC.
Orient a camera for horizontal viewing of the cylinder.
Place mice in separate beakers so they cannot see each other.
Dry each mouse thoroughly after swimming using paper towels and heat lamps placed near heating devices.
Use the same conditions on Day 2 as were used on Day 1.
Perform drug infusions in the morning on Day 2.
Place mice back into the water tanks four hours post-injection for another 15-minute session.
Record the behavior of the mice during the second swimming session.
Score the recorded behavior to quantify immobility time, defined as minimal movement necessary to keep the head above water.
Conduct a single forced swim test session for non-infused animals such as WT vs. HET mice.
Administer a second unilateral infusion one week after the initial FST in cannulated mice.
Monitor locomotor activity four hours post-second infusion using EthoVision pro software.
Calculate the distance traveled by each animal over a 10-minute period to quantify locomotor activity.
Place a sheet of poster board between two tanks so rats cannot see each other.
Display coded animal identification numbers on videotape for blind scoring.
Place animals in a plexiglass tank filled with water to a height of 50-60 cm for 15 minutes.
Repeat day 1 set up.
Perform infusions in the morning.
Four hours following drug or vehicle infusions, measure total number of beam breaks over 20 minutes.
Following locomotor activity assessment, perform the forced swim test by placing rats in a water tank and videotaping for 10 minutes.
Score animals for immobility, swimming, and climbing using a sampling technique to rate behavior over a 5 second interval (total 120 counts over 10 minutes).
Define immobility as absence of all movement except motions required to keep the head above water.
Define climbing as thrashing movements along the sides of the water tank.
Define swimming behavior as horizontal motion moving from one quadrant of the water tank to another.
Perform drug infusions in the morning.
Four hours post-infusion, administer a 6 minute tail suspension test.
Tape the tip of each tail using black electrical tape to a piece of Tygon tubing.
Suspend the animal above the floor at 60 cm.
Videotape the behavior.
Score the duration of immobility in 1-minute bins for 6 minutes.
Set lighting conditions to 40 lux (low lighting).
Place the animal in the center platform of the Elevated Plus Maze.
Videotape the behavior for 5 minutes.
Score entries into dark arms, entries into light arms, and time spent in light arms.
Perform the Open Field Test 2 days following the EPM.
Administer mouse infusions prior to placing them into the center of a Plexiglas box.
Record the distance moved and time spent in the entire open field or in a 25 cm x 25 cm center area using EthoVision pro video tracking system and software.
Allow mice to habituate by exposing them to sweetened milk in their home cage for ~1-2 hours sessions over 3 days.
Score latency to drink from the sweetened milk bottles in the home cage on the fourth day under dim lighting.
Perform drug infusions on the fifth day followed by measuring latencies to drink the sweetened milk in a novel cage under bright lighting.
Compare drinking latencies between the home cage and the novel cage.
